hook: A macro in an invoice. A laptop starts encrypting files. Every second counts.
stat: Ransomware was present in forty four percent of breaches in the latest Verizon report.
intro: Here is how Mova iO stops ransomware on one laptop, before it reaches the file shares.
s1: Microsoft Defender raises a high severity alert on a finance laptop. A Word document launched PowerShell, files in Documents are being renamed, and the device is reaching for a file share.
s2: Mova iO's triage agent reads the process tree and the timeline. Verdict: ransomware, ninety eight percent. For this pattern, the playbook says isolate first, then tell people.
s3: So the agent isolates the device straight away, while Teams and Outlook stay reachable. The SOC lead gets a notice in Teams, with a one-click release if it was wrong.
s4: Then it cleans up. A full scan runs, the malicious files are quarantined, and an investigation package is collected for the record.
s5: Next, it hunts across every device for the same file hash and the same macro. Nothing else is affected.
s6: In Intune, a fresh start is queued for the laptop, the user gets a loaner through ServiceNow, and the security incident closes with full evidence.
close: Ransomware stopped on one laptop. Isolated in under a minute. The rest of the estate checked and clean.
tag: Endpoint threats, stopped by Mova iO agents. With people in control.
end: Movate. Your applied A I partner.
